title: Early software
summary: This is a working prototype, not a finished product. Expect some rough edges.
paragraphs: My Own Suite is early software. It works — we build on it and run it ourselves — but it hasn't been hardened by years of production use, and some features have had limited real-world testing.

How it's built, plainly: much of the code was written with AI assistance. What that does not mean is code shipped unseen. No feature reaches a release before a human has driven it by hand on a real deployment — MOS is installed from scratch on virtual machines and on real cloud servers, over and over, and a large share of the work here has gone into the tooling that makes that verification repeatable rather than occasional.

The honest limit: that testing shows the software behaves correctly from the outside. It is not the same as a line-by-line human audit of every module, and we won't pretend it is. That audit is what an alpha is for — if the project proves its worth, every module goes through full verification by human engineers before we call it that.
callout: Practical advice for now: keep backups (MOS makes that easy), and don't make this the only copy of anything you'd hate to lose.
